body:
Submitted a fix in #25556.

Root cause confirmed from gateway logs: `kanban dispatcher: crashed=1` — the task crashed on `NoConsoleScreenBufferError` when prompt_toolkit tried to access a Win32 console buffer in the non-interactive kanban context.

Fix: catch the error in `_cprint` and fall back to plain `print()` so the kanban task continues running instead of crashing to Blocked status.

<!-- hermes-sweeper:item=25535 -->
<!-- hermes-sweeper:verdict=close reason=implemented_on_main confidence=high -->
This appears to be fixed on current `main` by the Windows redirected-stdout fallback in `_cprint`.

Automated hermes-sweeper review evidence:

- The reported traceback crashes while one-shot chat prints `Initializing agent...` through `_cprint` (`cli.py:9847`).
- Current `main` wraps that direct prompt_toolkit print path and falls back to plain `print(text)` when prompt_toolkit raises because stdout is not a real console; the inline comment explicitly calls out `NoConsoleScreenBufferError (Windows)` and subprocess worker logging (`cli.py:2224`).
- The implementation landed in `8bcb6082acf83db8e199f1065fa065340d82de0d` (`fix(windows): handle redirected stdout in _cprint fallback`), whose commit message describes the kanban-worker redirected stdout crash and fallback.
- The linked fix PR #25556 was also closed by a maintainer as already handled on `main`.

Thanks for the detailed report and logs; they line up with the fix that shipped after v0.13.0.
